summary:
I created an interactive animated story in Scratch 3 that brings the abandoned Apollo 11 Eagle Descent Stage back to life at Tranquility Base (0.67416° N, 23.47314° E). Through a timed conversation and liftoff animation featuring the Descent Stage, Neil Armstrong, and the departing spacecraft, the project explains what this historic hardware is, why it was left on the Moon on July 21, 1969 as a launchpad for the crew's safe return, and the scientific legacy it enabled—including the Lunar Laser Ranging Retro reflector still used by scientists today.
Built with authentic Apollo surface imagery and mission data from NASA’s Image and Video Library and Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) archives, this project transforms technical space history into an accessible narrative. It shows that while NASA’s lunar hardware rests silently in the regolith, its scientific contributions and cultural heritage remain vital to inspiring future Artemis explorers.
